title: Claude's auto-updater — is the logic baked into the model?
text: Someone assumes Claude's auto updater logic is baked into the model itself, some hidden capability. It isn't. It's baked into a file, skill.md. So, is the logic baked into the file?

title: SKILL.md is the file — the anchor
text: A Claude skill is just a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is named auto updater and everything it knows lives in one file, skill.md, plain sentences, not code. Open it and you'd see something like five numbered steps, top to bottom. Claude reads that file, then follows it. The file is the whole program. It can look like Claude is reasoning out

title: Linear, no hidden fallback
text: What to do on its own. That's the guess most people make. It isn't here. Claude works straight down the step section, one step after another, and only branches where a step actually says to. Delete step three from that file and step three simply doesn't happen. Nothing hidden fills the gap. Go back to

title: The anchor returns — same file, same result, then the edge
text: That same skill.md, the one with its steps listed top to bottom. Run auto updater on the same input twice and you get the same steps and the same result both times. That holds for as long as the input stays inside what the file describes. Step outside it into a case the file never anticipated and Claude has nothing written there to fall back on. title: Your turn
text: Prompt. Read it with me. Write me a skill.md with five short numbered steps for repeatable task I do often. Then read it back to me step by step before you run anything and follow only what's written, nothing else.
